@graph.schema:name: Carta Ontology
@graph.schema:description: A philosophical ontology for governance, identity, and capital — the machine-readable layer of Transition Insight (ashitmilne.xyz).

@graph.schema:name: Veritas
@graph.schema:description: Truth as the foundation for generative process — the basis from which utility and structural integrity are derived.

@graph.schema:name: Utilitas
@graph.schema:description: Utility — the generative process through which truth is transmuted into solutions and structural integrity in the real world.

@graph.schema:name: Firmitas
@graph.schema:description: Firmness — structural soundness and form aligned with nature; what good building yields when praxis and beta strengthen the trunk.

@graph.schema:name: Alpha
@graph.schema:description: Individual success along a chosen path — determined personal trajectory; the first element of the Triad.

@graph.schema:name: Beta
@graph.schema:description: Left-handed or unconventional departure point — the frontier for discovering genuine opportunity outside mainstream dogma.

@graph.schema:name: Omega
@graph.schema:description: Wholesome, internalized, integrative functionality — the holistically optimal outcome; the far shore beyond praxis on the S-curve of Areté.

@graph.schema:name: Carta
@graph.schema:description: Introductory essay establishing the ontology's foundational concepts: Soundness as structural integrity, the triadic model of Intelligence–Identity–Capital under Regnum Dei (Divine Governance), and the pursuit of alignment between Alpha and Omega.

@graph.schema:name: Canonical
@graph.schema:description: Comprehensive glossary framing foundational social-science concepts within the Carta ontology — original theoretical shorthand for navigating contested ideas across Intelligence, Identity, Capital, and Governance.

@graph.schema:name: Areté
@graph.schema:description: Virtue as the practice of turning the competitive impulse upon oneself to cultivate meaningful growth — the quality that enables contentment by deriving comfort from discomfort (hormesis).

@graph.schema:name: Semper Idem
@graph.schema:description: Semantic Perimeter of Identity Embodied — abstracted identity in the digital age manifested one transaction at a time, bounded by bricks and mortar yet functionally ephemeral.

@graph.schema:name: The Social Network
@graph.schema:description: The web of relationships among actors forming to provide safety, evolving from security-seeking to self-actualization — nodes, topology, Reed's Law, the Matthew Effect, and the path toward self-sovereign identity.

@graph.schema:name: Act I: अर्थ — Origins
@graph.schema:description: Autobiographical foundation tracing migration across three continents and the formation of an internationalist lens on political economy, keiretsu stakeholder capitalism, and the early internet.

@graph.schema:name: Act II: 気 — Trials of Job
@graph.schema:description: A quarter-century reckoning with moral injury at the nexus of information technology and political economy — the anarchist imperative for self-sovereignty and the derivation of order from personal cryptographic keys.

@graph.schema:name: Act III: πρᾶξις — Praxis
@graph.schema:description: Fluid practice that loosens orthodoxy to explore the edge — the arc from rigid Project through continuous Product to decentralized Protocol, reclaiming self-sovereignty through cryptographic custody.

@graph.schema:name: Connexion
@graph.schema:description: Transparent gateway for direct contact — embodying the ontology's principle of openness and unmediated interface between identities.

@graph.schema:name: One Step Beyond — The Making of Ashit Milne
@graph.schema:description: The coming-together of identity through synchronicity, yoga practice, and the adoption of a name embodying vitality and convergence — Milne as the seed of mission.

@graph.schema:name: Macauley's Favorite Bastard — The Making of Ashit Patel
@graph.schema:description: Origins of identity as a tel — stratified mound of civilisational sediment, from colonial East Africa through England and India to Canada; the etymology of Patel as ledger-keeper.

@graph.schema:name: The Transition
@graph.schema:description: Breathwork as metaphor for civilisational evolution — from dharana through dhyana to samadhi; the passage from extractive hierarchy toward protocol-secured custody of identity and capital.

@graph.schema:name: The Tenable
@graph.schema:description: Money and interaction fit for good-faith increments — the imperative to make currency and conduct tenable at civilisational scale, governed by personal authority rather than the caprice of giants.
